messages:
kim (support): FYI customer AcmeHealth just escalated — they see quota/rate-limit failures but our API is returning 5xx instead of 429. They had a production outage. They want an ETA.
sam (eng-sre): ack, can you paste one example request/response and approximate timeline?
ellie (support): reported ~09:12-09:18 UTC. cURL from their logs: 
``` 
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \ 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-acme-XXXXX' \ 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ 
  -d '{"model":"rwd-large-1","input":"hi"}'
```
Response headers/snippet: `HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error` and body `{ "error": "quota service unavailable" }`
kim (support): they say this should've been `429 Too Many Requests` because they exceeded quota. Downstream client logic treats 5xx as unknown and retries, amplifying the issue.
sam (eng-sre): initial triage steps I've run: checked gateway/error rates, saw spike in 5xx for route `/v1/generate` starting 09:10 UTC. scope=quota-checker. Running `kubectl logs -l app=quota-gateway -n prod --since=1h | grep -i "timeout\|error\|429"` shows a lot of `upstream timeout` and then `returning 500`.
maria (eng-runtime): adding context — we rolled quota-orchestrator v2.3.0 yesterday (canary). It added a dependency call to auth-cache that has longer tail. If that dependency times out, the orchestrator sometimes returns a generic 500 instead of mapping to 429 or a controlled 503.
dan (oncall): is there a short-term mitigation we can flip (traffic reroute / config) to stop 5xx and return 429 or synthetic 429 for known customers?
sam (eng-sre): yes — two options: 1) route traffic to the previous stable quota-orchestrator (rollback canary), 2) enable 'fail-soft' mode in quota-gateway config which converts dependency timeouts to `429` for non-critical clients. I have a patch ready.
kim (support): customer wants immediate mitigation; prefer minimal blast radius. Which is faster?
sam (eng-sre): enabling fail-soft is a single flag in the feature flag service and updates the gateway config via our control plane — ~5 min to rollout. Rolling back canary needs a canary deploy -> 10-15 min. I'll do fail-soft now.
sam (eng-sre): `ffctl set --env=prod quota.fail_soft true --actor=sam`
deploy-bot: @sam scheduled feature-flag change `quota.fail_soft=true` for prod by sam at 09:25 UTC, rolling to 100% in 2 minutes.
sam (eng-sre): pushed, watching metrics.

maria (eng-runtime): posting observed log excerpt from quota-orchestrator right before the spike: 
```
2026-03-10T09:11:03Z ERROR orchestrator request_id=abc123 upstream=auth-cache timeout after=2500ms
2026-03-10T09:11:03Z ERROR orchestrator request_id=abc123 returning 500 unexpected error while mapping quota
```
dan (oncall): metrics update — 1 minute after flag: 5xx rate dropped by ~85%, 429 increased as expected. Customer confirmed retries stopped.
ellie (support): relayed to AcmeHealth: temporary mitigation applied, we will follow up with a root-cause and permanent fix. They asked for postmortem and a timeline.
sam (eng-sre): root cause hypothesis: auth-cache introduced tail latency; orchestrator didn't have a robust mapping on dependency timeout -> should surface 429/429-like behavior. Also a routing rule in front of orchestrator wasn't honoring the 'fail_soft' boolean in some edge cases (that's why we saw 500s).
maria (eng-runtime): reproducer for devs (safe steps):
1) set local env `QUOTA_ORCH_TIMEOUT_MS=50`
2) run the integration script `./dev/local_send.sh --apikey test-acme`
3) in logs you should see `upstream timeout` then `500 returned` instead of `429`

maria (eng-runtime): sample unit test we will add to prevent regression: 
```
it "maps dependency timeout to quota response" do
  allow(dependency).to receive(:check).and_raise(Timeout::Error)
  expect(response.status).to eq(429)
end
```
sam (eng-sre): action plan (short): 
- revert canary / patch orchestrator to map timeouts -> 429 (maria) (owner: maria)
- add unit/integration test (maria)
- extend tracing for quota flows (nate)
- update runbook to include fast FF toggle for fail_soft (sam)
- notify customers and PM (kim)

maria (eng-runtime): I'll open PR to map TimeoutError -> QuotaExceededError and add tests. Targeting hotfix release in ~2h.
nate (sre): I'll add a tracing span in the quota path and set alert if dependency tail > 2000ms and if we start converting timeouts to 500.
dan (oncall): postmortem owners? maria (root), sam (mitigation/runbook), nate (monitoring). I'll create the incident ticket and assign.

kim (support): customer follow-up note: "Thanks — we saw the service come back quickly after your config change. Please confirm fix and ETA for permanent patch."
sam (eng-sre): confirmed we will push hotfix + tests and then roll canary with stricter timeout mapping. ETA ~2 hours for hotfix, 6 hours for monitored canary.
deploy-bot: @maria created rollout job `quota-orch-hotfix` at 09:46 UTC, canary=10% -> hold.

maria (eng-runtime): quick note — we should also adjust client-side guidance: treat 5xx from quota endpoint as transient for now and prefer exponential backoff, but after hotfix they should expect 429 for quota. I'll add to developer docs.

sam (eng-sre): leaving timeline & next steps in incident ticket. Closing slack loop for now; will post when hotfix lands. :white_check_mark:
kim (support): thanks everyone — keeping customer updated. :heart:
